Bakertilly._comment: Bangalore site, one counter, TWO non-veg dishes (themes Mon/Thu = mix, Tue = south, Wed = biryani, Fri = north). The non-veg station runs EVERY day with ONE dish, and a SECOND dish is added on the biryani day where both are chicken dry — the client's latest clarification, which replaces the earlier reading that the station stood down entirely on the other four days. Its biryani-day list ('indian bread, rasam, veg curry, flavoured rice, white rice and salad — other will be blank') and its curd rule ('daily curd except of biryani day it is raita') disagree about the curd on a Wednesday; the client called that an outlier, so `curd_side` is KEPT there as a raita and nothing else is inferred from the conflict. 'Daily curd except on the biryani day it is raita' is the city ruleset's `curd_raita_logic` and is not restated here.

rules._comment: 'On biryani day we will only serve indian bread, rasam, veg curry, flavoured rice, white rice and salad — other will be blank.' Wednesday is this counter's biryani day, so the veg dry, dal, sambar and dessert stations stand down there. `nonveg_main` is the mirror image — it runs ONLY on Wednesday (see below) — and `curd_side` is kept per the header comment.
rules.name: bakertilly_no_veg_dry_on_biryani_day

rules._comment: 'Non veg 2 will come only on biryani day, and 1' — TWO non-veg dishes on Wednesday and ONE on every other day. This REPLACES the earlier reading that the whole station stood down Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri; that dropped the base slot outright and left those days with no non-veg at all. `slot_indices` stands down only the SECOND expansion, so `nonveg_main__1` is solved every day and `nonveg_main__2` exists on Wednesday alone — the same mechanism TCL uses to run one flavoured rice on Saturday and two the rest of the week, and the same shape a client constant uses to pin `__2` while `__1` still solves.
rules.name: bakertilly_second_nonveg_on_the_biryani_day_only

rules._comment: …'and it will be chicken dry'. Both Wednesday cells are dry, so `count: 2` over the two dry flags. The city rule `nonveg_main_daily_pair` is DISABLED for this client rather than overridden: it composes a 2-4 dish counter as one dry plus one regional chicken gravy, and on a biryani day as biryani plus gravy — both of which put a gravy on the plate the client says is dry. `count` caps itself to what the day can serve, so if the biryani-day pool offers only one dry the component relaxes to one and diagnose() reports it (the theme filter keeps the dry families available at 2+ slots — CLAUDE.md note 16).
rules.name: bakertilly_two_chicken_dry_on_the_biryani_day

rules._comment: 'Need a veg gravy (paneer, baby corn, gobi, mushroom, rajma, chole, channa) all day, first priority.' The counter serves ONE veg gravy, so a one-slot component with count 1 IS 'this slot must be a matching dish' (note 20) — and a composition component RELAXES rather than failing when a day cannot supply one, which is what makes it a first priority rather than an ultimatum. 388 of Bangalore's 1,184 veg gravies match, so a daily slot has depth to spare against the 20-day cooldown. Paneer is selected on `primary_protein` and the NAME, never `key_ingredient`: that column is the de-facto default for a Chinese dish here, which is why a Thai green curry used to read as a paneer gravy (scripts/definitional_flags.py). Compatible with the city's `premium_veg_gravy_exactly_one` — only 19 of the 388 carry `is_premium_gravy`, leaving 369 non-premium options for the other four days — and with `bakertilly_paneer_1x`, which caps the paneer share of it at one day.
rules.name: bakertilly_veg_gravy_from_the_named_families_daily
